passages.context: Meehan defines the sacristy by its storage, assembly, and vesting functions. His furnishing paragraph names a crucifix or other suitable image in a prominent position for the departure and return bow, a lavatory for handwashing, and, as customary, a holy-water font and a bell at the door leading to the sanctuary to admonish the congregation of the clergy's advent. This controls a dated specialist description and local/usual recognition only; it does not establish a universal 1962 furnishing code, a bell mechanism or operator, or a prescribed lavatory form.

work.description: The thirteenth volume (1912) of the sixteen-volume Catholic Encyclopedia (New York: Robert Appleton Company, 1907-1912). Signed articles are cited by article title; the volume's container identity remains distinct from each contributor's article. Herbert Thurston's articles 'The Rosary' (with Andrew Shipman for the Eastern section) and 'Feast of the Holy Rosary' belong to this volume.
